The CDC noted a significant increase in vaccine exemption requests, which may be linked to the recent outbreaks. The measles virus belongs to the Morbillivirus family and is known to cause severe health issues, including pneumonia and brain swelling.

analysis.brief_en: Two unvaccinated residents of Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, have died from measles, marking the first U.S. measles-associated fatalities in 2026 and Pennsylvania’s first such deaths in 35 years, state health officials reported on August 25. Pennsylvania alone has tallied 393 cases across 28 counties. CDC data show kindergarten MMR vaccination coverage fell to 92.4% in 2025–2026 from 95.2% in 2019–2020, leaving roughly 280,000 children without full protection. Measles can lead to severe complications, including pneumonia and brain inflammation, with hospitalization in about one in five patients and death in 1–3 per 1,000 cases.

title: Measles Kills Two in Lancaster County: Pennsylvania Records First Deaths in 35 Years - Tech Times

analysis.time: The measles outbreak in Pennsylvania was reported in 2026, with the two deaths occurring in Lancaster County on Tuesday, as noted in N2. The vaccination rate decline was observed over eight years, with the 2025–26 school year showing a significant drop to 87.6% (N9). The national MMR vaccination rate was at 92.4% in 2026 (N19).
analysis.location_and_population: The event occurred in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, affecting unvaccinated residents. The county's kindergarten measles vaccination rate fell to 87.6% in 2025–26, leaving more than one in eight children unprotected (N9). The outbreak spread across 29 counties in Pennsylvania, with 393 confirmed cases and 70 hospitalizations statewide (N6).
analysis.event: Two unvaccinated residents in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, died from measles, marking the first measles-associated deaths in the U.S. in 2026 and the first in the state in 35 years (N2). The Pennsylvania Department of Health confirmed these deaths (N3).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The outbreak resulted in 393 confirmed cases in Pennsylvania, with 20% hospitalized and none fully vaccinated (N20). analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Public health officials and physicians criticized the federal policy changes that undermined vaccination infrastructure (N27).
